title: Optimize NCCL stream scheduling and kernel-sync for tensor-parallel overlap
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were suffering from suboptimal overlap between communication and compute, especially on long-sequence inference where NVLink/NIC bandwidth and kernel launch syncs dominated latency. This PR changes NCCL stream ordering and kernel synchronization points, introduces a lightweight scheduling heuristic in the stream scheduler, and adds kernel-side flags to allow asynchronous collectives where safe. The goals are to increase comm/compute overlap, reduce idle kernels waiting on NCCL ops, and avoid unnecessary stream syncs that serialized execution. High level changes: 1) New prioritized stream pool for NCCL collectives with configurable priorities per-device and per-collective type. 2) Adjusted ordering for AllReduce/AllGather launches to submit comm work on high-priority streams before kernel launches, enabling device-side overlap. 3) Introduced an opt-in kernel flag (allow_async_collective) for layers that are proven safe to continue compute while comm completes. 4) Improvements to the scheduler to detect small kernels that should yield to ongoing collectives (short-kernel yielding). 5) Tweaks to KV cache invalidation to avoid blocking collectives when serving multistream batched requests. 6) New perf tests and microbench harness for tensor-parallel collectives and overlap measurement. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless server config or model profile enables the new priority pool or layer flags. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind runtime flag enable_tp_overlap_opt (off by default), start with internal canary on dedicated clusters, monitor per-route latency P50/P95 and GPU utilization. Benchmarks: on internal 8xA100 TP-8 runs with 2048 context the changes improved mean token latency by 12-18% and reduced stall time on GPU by ~22% for common LLaMA-like models. Testing: added unit tests for stream ordering, integration perf tests measuring overlap, and end-to-end regression tests against existing model outputs to ensure no correctness regressions. See linked Linear tasks for risk assessment and rollout steps.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2026-02-16): Can you explain how priority inversion is avoided when multiple collectives compete for the high-priority pool?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): We cap the number of concurrent high-priority streams per-device and fall back to fair scheduling when the cap is hit. Added comment and unit test covering this behavior.
Lena Chen (2026-02-17): The allow_async_collective flag looks risky for correctness. What validation do you perform?

Aisha Patel (2026-02-17): The flag is opt-in at the model-profile layer. We validate with deterministic ref-run regression tests that compare outputs after moving comm earlier. Added integration tests that run with and without the flag to assert identical outputs for supported layers.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-18): Observability: please add metrics that show overlap percentage and stall time per device so we can monitor rollout.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-18): Added metrics runtime.tp.collective_overlap_pct and runtime.tp.gpu_stall_ms and wired them to the console dashboard.
testing_summary: Unit tests for stream ordering and kernel flags added. Integration perf harness measures overlap gain. Deterministic regression tests run across 10 models at multiple sequence lengths. Internal canary on dedicated cluster validated correctness and latency improvements. No model output regressions detected in the opt-in cases.
benchmarks: 8xA100 TP-8 LLaMA-like model at 2k context: mean token latency down 12-18%, GPU idle/stall time down ~22%, throughput improved by ~7% under mixed batch sizes. Microbench AllGather/AllReduce overlap increased by 30-40% on average.
release_notes: Improve NCCL stream scheduling and kernel synchronization to increase communication/compute overlap for tensor-parallel workloads. Opt-in runtime flag enable_tp_overlap_opt controls rollout. Expected improvements: lower token latency and reduced GPU stall time for multi-GPU tensor-parallel models.
